grammar.title: 不用 for "no need to"
grammar.explanation: 不用 (búyòng) means there's no need to do something — softer than telling someone not to with 别. 不用了，谢谢 ("No need, thanks") is a common way to politely decline an offer.

grammar.title: Resultative complements with 到 and 见
grammar.explanation: Adding 到 (dào) or 见 (jiàn) right after a verb shows the action succeeded, not just that it was attempted: 找到 ("found", not just "looked for"), 看见 ("saw", not just "looked at"), 听到 ("heard"), 回到 ("made it back to"). Without the complement, 看 and 听 only describe the effort, not the outcome.

sentences.en: You don't need to do it.
